title: epan: Remove STR_ASCII and STR_UNICODE
description:
These display bases work to replace unprintable characters, which
is a misnomer, they are the same option and this is not something
that is configurable.

All our internal text strings need to be valid UTF-8.

Remove the assertion because tvb_get_*_string() must return a
valid UTF-8 string, always, and we don't need to assert that,
it is expensive.

notes.body: If there's no meaning left in that parameter, might as well fall back to the default: `BASE_NONE` ?
I would prefer not. BASE_NONE for string types seems extra confusing, and doesn't fit the existing patterns.

How do you like this latest version?

The name of the field in a `header_field_info` that holds the `BASE_` values is `display`, not `base` - "base" is a historical artifact from when *only* numerical fields had an option for how they should be displayed, and the option was "base 10, base 8, or base 16".

Perhaps `DISPLAY_STR_NONE` instead?  (Or `DISPLAY_STR_DEFAULT`?)

Then another change might be to replace `BASE_` with `DISPLAY_`, and prepend `DISPLAY_` to the `STR_` values, with #defines for the old names kept around for backwards compatibility.
Yes, I agree it's a better name. It was my first choice but then I changed it. I will do that.
Actually the name should just be `DISPLAY_NONE`, not `DISPLAY_BASE_NONE`, `DISPLAY_STR_NONE`, `DISPLAY_SEP_NONE`, etc.

commits_data.message:
epan: Remove STR_ASCII and STR_UNICODE

These display bases work to replace unprintable characters so the
name is a misnomer. In addition they are the same option and this
display behaviour is not something that is configurable.

This does not affect encodings because all our internal text strings
need to be valid UTF-8 and the source encoding is specified using
ENC_*.

Remove the assertion for valid UTF-8 in proto.c because
tvb_get_*_string() must return a valid UTF-8 string, always, and we
don't need to assert that, it is expensive.
